en: I see, I see.
I'm Hugo,
and a stroll like this is my daily routine.
Next time we meet, let's have a nice, easy chat.
Don't be absurd!
I have no time to waste on strolls!
You're an odd one too. Busy as you are,
you stop to talk to an old codger like me.
and I take a stroll like this every day.
Come talk to me again when you're not busy.
Want to keep me company on my stroll, eh?
I'm out on my stroll again today.
I watch the port from the lighthouse daily.
, it's you.
note: NAME + ', it's you. ' + #4795/#4816 (both start with a capital)

en: I'm out strolling again today, same as ever.
I keep watch over the monument every day.
Evening to you.
You want to come over to my place, do you?
I'm on my way back from my stroll again.
Heading home from my stroll, same as ever.
A visitor for an old codger like me? How rare.
I'm Hugo. I used to keep the lighthouse.
And what's your name?

note: Duran's curt reply 'NAME.'; also closes M1#6654 in msg 271258 ('...I am / NAME.')

en: That's a tricky name.
note: leading space: follows NAME + M1#777 variant ', is it?' (msgs 189363, 190363)

en: Well, pleased to meet you.
, it's you. Good of you to come.
Now, stay and have a cup of tea.
Come visit again anytime.
What is it? Did you forget something?
Or maybe
there's something on this old geezer's face?
Now, stay and have some sweets.
Sorry, what we had earlier was the last
of my tea and sweets.
Come visit again tomorrow or so.
What are you doing here?
Hm, are you talking to me?
I'm not doing anything in particular.
I'm just staring into space.
This monument, you see, was a lighthouse
until just recently. I worked there as its
keeper...
I prayed for safe voyages and watched over
many a ship, but now my life comes down to
just looking at this monument.
Old soldiers just fade away, as they say.
What are you doing here?
Hm, you still want to talk with me?
I've got a few things I want to think over.
I'd be glad if you'd come back tomorrow.
When I'd only just started keeping the light,
Calstatt was still a small town.
Even so, there was a lot of ship traffic.
Looking back, I suppose that was just when
the town began to grow.
Most of the ships coming into port carried
iron, coal and the like. With those, in no
time at all this town's industry took off.
I'm sure it wasn't just Calstatt, either.
Other towns must have gone the same way.
Have you been to the west side of the port?
There are navy barracks there.
Those were only built recently.
Ever since that Bismarck fellow resigned,
the ships coming to port suddenly changed.
Ships carrying iron and coal fell off fast,
and trade ships and warships grew common.
There's a dock at the far west of the harbor,
and I hear that next year it'll be reborn
as a navy dock.
Left behind by the great changes of the age,
the lighthouse and I now just stand like this
in a corner of town, and nothing more.
The lighthouse has become a monument.
Why not be reborn yourself, then?
Could someone like me really be reborn?
I can't help feeling that for this old codger,
there's nothing left ahead but death.
No... I can't be reborn after all.
